paragraphs: The 520i has been part of the 5 Series range since 2010, and across its three generations has used two different four-cylinder petrol engines — from the N20 through to today's B48. Early F10/F11 cars (2010–2017) use the N20, a 2.0-litre turbocharged four-cylinder. From 2017 onwards, the G30/G31 and current G60 generations switched to the B48, a more recent engine that's part of BMW's modular B-series family. The full breakdown by engine code is below.
about.boldParagraph: The 520i is no longer in production, but we continue to rebuild and replace engines for every one still on the road.

cards.body: A 2.0-litre turbocharged four-cylinder petrol fitted to the 520i during the F10/F11 generation. Known for timing chain guide wear over time — see the callout above. We replace the timing chain, guides, tensioners and gaskets as standard on every N20 rebuild.

A 2.0-litre turbocharged four-cylinder petrol fitted to the 520i during the G30/G31 generation. B-series engines are generally reliable — we service it to the same standard as our other 520i rebuilds.

The current 2.0-litre turbocharged four-cylinder petrol fitted to the 520i in the G60 generation. Too new for a real-world pattern to exist — we service it to the same standard as our other 520i rebuilds.

compatibility.intro: Because the 520i spans two distinct engines across three generations, fitting the wrong replacement — or assuming an N20 part will work on a B48 car — risks a compatibility problem that's expensive to unpick. Before we quote or supply anything, we confirm:

points.text: Your exact engine code (N20 or B48) via registration or VIN
Any electronics or ECU considerations specific to your exact build

compatibility.footer: This is why we always start with your registration rather than a generic 520i quote — it protects you from paying for parts that don't fit your actual car.
